summary: The video documents converting a two‑unit heating setup—a gas-fired cast‑iron boiler plus a separate domestic hot water heater—into a single, compact gas-fired combination boiler (combi) that provides both space heating and domestic hot water. It explains how a flat plate heat exchanger within the combi substitutes the large iron block, how the system modulates to match load, and why venting, condensate handling, and proper sizing are critical. The host and installer emphasize efficiency gains, on‑demand hot water, and the practical limits of a combi unit (house size and DHW demand), along with exterior venting requirements and code-based clearances.

sections.description: The system described uses a separate cast-iron boiler for space heating and a separate gas-fired storage-type water heater for domestic hot water. The boiler heats a large volume of water in a cast-iron block, and a circulator moves heated water to convectors upstairs while exhaust exits via a chimney.

sections.description: The combi has a small stainless steel block with a circulator that heats water, which then transfers heat to the domestic water via a flat plate heat exchanger. This design enables on-demand hot water without a storage tank.

sections.description: To accommodate the combi’s efficient venting needs, two openings to the outdoors are planned. The crew highlights a favorable sidewall location, with the intake and exhaust positioned apart and screened, and notes code-based requirements such as staying above snow line, keeping a 12-inch distance from windows, and at least one foot between intake and exhaust.

sections.title: Condensing boiler fundamentals and DHW priority
concepts: modulating gas valve (range: 75,000–177,000 BTU)

sections.description: The unit is a condensing boiler with a modulating gas valve that scales output to match demand, controlled by an outdoor sensor. It uses a flat-plate exchanger to heat potable water and captures condensate with a neutralizer and pump. When a hot water tap is opened, DHW is prioritized.

sections.title: Limitations and practical considerations
concepts: house size and available power affect combi suitability
DHW capacity constraints (e.g., large tubs 80–100 gallons)
sections.description: The host discusses limitations of combi systems: they are best for appropriately sized homes and typical DHW demand; very large tub fills or oversized homes may not be ideal for a single combi unit.
